text_es: Create an HTML invoice generator with the main function invoice(data). Start by creating a header string containing the invoice number and customer name. Create a table start string using the word table. Iterate over the items to create table rows. For each item, format a string for the item description, a string for the quantity, a string for the unit price formatted to two decimals, and a string for the calculated subtotal. After the loop, format a string for the grand total row. Close the table with a closing string. Create a footer string thanking the customer by name. Return an array of all the generated HTML strings.

Implement a markdown builder with the function profile(user). The input object has fields for username, full name, location, age, occupation, website, and a list of hobbies. Generate a main heading string with the full name and username. Generate a subheading string for the location and age. Create a string for the occupation section. Format a link string for the website. Create a string starting a list of hobbies. Iterate through the hobbies and create a formatted list item string for each hobby name. Format a footer string with the current year and username. Format a contact string with a simulated email address based on the username and a default domain. Return a single joined string separated by newlines.

Create an email campaign generator with the function campaign(details). The input provides a recipient name, a product name, a discount percentage, a promo code, an expiration date, and a sender name. Generate a subject line string featuring the product name and discount percentage. Format a greeting string using the recipient name. Create a string introducing the product name. Format a string highlighting the promo code and the discount percentage. Create a string mentioning the expiration date. Format a call to action string with a fabricated web link containing the promo code. Generate a sign off string using the sender name. Create a footer string with an unsubscribe link containing the recipient name. Return an array of the email lines.

Write a function dockerfile(config) that generates lines for a container build file. The input contains a base image, a maintainer name, an application directory, an environment variable, an exposed port, a start command, and a package to install. Generate a from string using the base image. Format a maintainer string with the maintainer name. Create a work directory string using the application directory. Format an environment string setting the environment variable to the word production. Generate a run string to update and install the specified package. Format a copy string for the application files. Create an expose string using the exposed port. Generate a command string using the start command. Return the lines as an array of strings.

Implement a style generator using stylesheet(theme). The input object contains primary color, secondary color, base font size, heading font size, margin size, padding size, and border radius. Generate a string for the body selector setting the background to the primary color. Format a string for text color using the secondary color. Create a string for paragraph font size using the base font size. Format a string for heading size using the heading font size. Generate a string for a container class setting the margin to the margin size. Create a string for the container padding using the padding size. Format a string for button border radius using the border radius. Format a string for a hover state pseudo class using the primary color. Return the generated rules as an array of strings.

Create a function graph(network) to generate a directed graph representation in the dot language. The input has a graph name, an array of node objects each with an identifier and a label, and an array of edge objects each with a source, destination, and weight. Format a string to start a directed graph using the graph name. Iterate through the nodes and format a string for each assigning the label to the identifier. Iterate through the edges and format a string for each connecting the source to the destination. Inside the edge loop format a string to set the weight label. Format a string to set a default node shape to the word circle. Format a string to set a default edge color to the word blue. Format a string to close the graph structure. Format a string describing the total count of nodes and edges as a comment. Return all strings as an array.

Implement execute(options) to build command line execution strings for a media encoder. The input contains an input file, an output file, a video codec, an audio codec, a bitrate, a resolution, and a preset. Format a string for the basic executable command. Create a string for the input file flag using the input file path. Format a string for the video codec flag. Generate a string for the audio codec flag. Create a string for the bitrate parameter. Format a string for the resolution scale parameter. Create a string for the preset speed flag. Generate a string for the output file path. Return an array of all these flag strings.

Implement a function makefile(build) that creates build instructions for a software project. The input provides a compiler name, compiler flags, a target executable name, a source directory, an object directory, and an installation path. Format a string to define the compiler variable using the compiler name. Create a string for the flags variable using the compiler flags. Format a string for the target rule using the target executable name. Generate a string for compiling source files from the source directory into the object directory. Create a string for the clean rule targeting the object directory. Format a string for an install rule using the target executable name and the installation path. Generate a string for an uninstall rule removing the target from the installation path. Format a string listing phony targets. Return an array of these configuration strings.

Implement a function proxy(server) that creates reverse proxy configuration lines. The input provides a domain name, a listen port, a backend upstream address, a log file path, an ssl certificate path, and an ssl key path. Format a string for the server block opening. Create a string to set the listen directive using the listen port. Format a string for the server name directive using the domain name. Generate a string for the access log directive using the log file path. Create a string for the ssl certificate directive using the ssl certificate path. Format a string for the ssl key directive using the ssl key path. Generate a string for the location block forwarding requests to the backend upstream address. Format a string setting a proxy header with the domain name. Return an array of these configuration strings.

Write a function `policy(rules)` that accepts a list of rule objects. Each rule object has a resource string, an action list, and an effect string. The function must build an access control policy document string manually. It should have a helper to format the version header, a helper to format each statement block with its specific actions, and a main driver that joins them. Build distinct strings for the policy header, the version declaration, the statement array opening, the statement identifier line, the effect declaration, the action array opening, the specific action items, the resource line, and the closing brackets. Example input: a list with one rule for an object bucket and read actions. Output: a properly indented string containing the entire policy statement.

Create a function `hook(config)` that generates a pre commit bash script. The configuration object contains a project name, a linter command, a branch prefix, and a warning message. Create helpers to build the header, the branch checking logic which compares the current branch against the allowed prefix, and the linting execution block. You must construct separate strings for the bash header, the strict mode declaration, the branch variable assignment, the branch check condition, the branch error message, the lint command variable, the lint execution block, and the lint error output. Example input: a project named frontend, branch prefix feature, and a code formatting command. Output: a complete bash script as a string.

Write a function `alerts(thresholds)` that accepts a list of monitoring definitions. Each definition contains a metric name, a warning limit, a critical limit, and an application identifier. Create helpers to generate the rule group header, the warning alert definition, and the critical alert definition. Assemble distinct strings for the group name declaration, the evaluation interval, the warning alert name, the warning expression, the warning duration, the warning labels, the critical alert name, the critical expression, and the critical annotations. Example input: a memory metric with a warning limit of eighty and critical of ninety for an app named backend. Output: a formatted monitoring rules string.

Provide a function `manifest(service)` that produces a deployment and networking string for a containerized application. The service object includes an application name, a container image, a port number, and a replica count. Write helper functions to generate the deployment metadata block, the pod template specification, and the networking service block. You will need to construct strings for the api version headers, the resource kind declarations, the metadata name line, the application labels, the replicas count, the container name, the container image definition, the port mappings, and the selector matches. Example input: an app named web using a proxy image with port eighty and two replicas. Output: a single string with both manifests separated by dashes.

Provide a function `schema(models)` that takes a list of data model definitions to produce a complete type definition string. Each model has a name, a description, and a list of property objects containing a name, a type, and a required flag. Create helpers to generate the type declaration header, the individual field lines, and a root query type. Construct separate strings for the schema opening, the type documentation comment, the type declaration line, the required field definition, the optional field definition, the root query wrapper, the query resolver signature, and the schema closing. Example input: a user model with a required identifier and an optional alias. Output: a formatted schema definition string.

Implement a function `session(layout)` that generates a shell script to automate a terminal multiplexer setup. The layout object defines a session name, a base directory, and a list of window objects each containing a name and a startup command. Write helpers to generate the session initialization command, the window creation commands, and the command execution lines. You will build strings for the bash shebang, the session existence check, the new session creation, the target directory change, the new window creation, the window renaming command, the send keys execution, and the final session attach directive. Example input: a session named dev with two windows running an editor and a server. Output: a bash script string that starts the environment.

Provide a function `sitemap(pages)` that generates an XML document for search engines. The pages list contains objects that have a relative path, a priority number, and an update frequency string. Write helpers to output the standard XML declaration, the URL set opening tag, and the individual URL entries. Construct strings for the XML declaration header, the URL set opening tag, the URL wrapper opening, the full location path, the priority tag, the change frequency tag, the last modified date tag, the URL wrapper closing, and the URL set closing. Example input: a list with a home page at the root path and a contact page. Output: a full XML document string.

Write a function `contacts(people)` that generates a virtual contact file string from a list of user profiles. Each profile contains a first name, a last name, a phone number, an email address, and an organization name. Implement helpers to construct the begin tags, the formatted name properties, the telephone properties, the email properties, and the organization properties. Build distinct strings for the begin card tag, the version declaration, the full name line, the structured name line, the work phone line, the home phone line, the internet email line, the organization property, and the end card tag. Example input: a list of one person named john doe working at a factory. Output: a text string conforming to the standard contact format.

Implement a function `diagram(interactions)` that outputs a text based sequence diagram string. The interactions list holds objects with a sender, a receiver, a message, and a synchronous flag. Create helpers to generate the diagram start tag, the participant definitions, the message arrows which differ based on the synchronous flag, and the diagram end tag. Construct strings for the start tag, the title declaration, the actor participant declaration, the database participant declaration, the solid arrow for synchronous calls, the dotted arrow for asynchronous calls, the message labels, the activation block, and the end tag. Example input: a client sending a request to a server synchronously, then the server logging asynchronously. Output: a complete diagram script.

Provide a function `service(config)` that builds an initialization unit file. The configuration object includes a unit description, an execution path, a working directory, a user name, and an environment profile. Write helpers to construct the unit section, the service section, and the install section. Build strings for the unit section header, the description line, the after network dependency, the service section header, the execution start command, the working directory path, the user assignment, the environment file include, and the wanted by target. Example input: a node application running under a dedicated user account. Output: a standard unit file string.

Write a function `vhost(domain)` that creates a web server configuration block. The domain object contains a server name, an alias list, a document root path, and an admin email. Implement helpers to format the virtual host opening tag, the server identity lines, the directory access controls, and the logging paths. Generate separate strings for the virtual host opening tag, the port eighty binding, the server name directive, the server alias list, the server admin line, the document root assignment, the directory allow override directive, the error log path, and the custom log path. Example input: a primary domain example com with an alias. Output: a multi line configuration string.

Provide a function `ticket(issue)` that formats a markdown description for a bug tracking system. The issue object includes a title, an environment string, a reporter name, a list of reproduction steps, and an expected behavior. Write helpers to construct the header block, the environment table, the numbered steps list, and the conclusion section. Generate distinct strings for the primary heading, the reporter metadata line, the operating system row, the browser version row, the reproduction steps header, the numbered step item lines, the expected behavior header, the expected behavior block, and the actual behavior block. Example input: a login bug reported by an administrator with three reproduction steps. Output: a markdown formatted document.

Write a function `backup(job)` that produces a shell script for synchronizing directories. The job object defines a source path, a destination host, a destination path, a secure key file, and an exclude pattern. Create helpers to build the script header, the logging setup, the synchronization command, and the completion notification. Build distinct strings for the bash interpreter line, the strict error handling line, the log file definition, the source path variable, the destination path variable, the secure shell command argument, the exclusion flag, the main synchronization command, and the completion success message. Example input: a job backing up a user home directory to a remote server. Output: a bash script string.

Implement a function `firewall(policies)` that generates a shell script to configure network rules. The policies list contains objects with a protocol, a port number, a source ip range, and an action like accept or drop. Write helpers to construct the flush existing rules command, the default policy commands, and the specific port rules. Construct separate strings for the interpreter shebang, the flush existing rules command, the default input drop line, the default forward drop line, the default output accept line, the loopback accept rule, the specific protocol flag, the destination port flag, and the jump action flag. Example input: a policy allowing connections from a specific local network. Output: a complete configuration script string.

Provide a function `aggregation(query)` that formats a database query pipeline into a readable code string for documentation purposes. The query object has a match collection name, a group field, a sum alias, and a sort order. Create helpers to build the match stage string, the group stage string, and the sort stage string. Construct strings for the collection pipeline wrapper, the match stage opening, the match condition syntax, the group stage opening, the group identifier mapping, the accumulator function syntax, the sort stage opening, the sort direction line, and the array closing brackets. Example input: a query filtering active users and grouping them by region. Output: a string representation of the pipeline.

Write a function `schedule(tasks)` that creates a system task file string. The tasks list contains objects with minute, hour, day, month, and weekday expressions, along with an execution command and an output log file. Implement helpers to generate the environment variable header, the individual task schedule lines, and the output redirection logic. Build distinct strings for the shell environment assignment, the path variable assignment, the mail notification assignment, the task comment description, the timing expression columns, the command execution path, the standard output redirection, the error output redirection, and the newline separator. Example input: a daily cleanup script running at midnight. Output: a formatted schedule file string.

Write a module to generate a basic typesetting markup document from a content specification. Provide `typeset(document)`. The document object contains a paper size, an author, a title, an abstract text, and a list of sections. Each section has a heading and an array of paragraphs. The output must begin with a document class declaration using the paper size. Next, output the title declaration and author declaration. Begin the document environment. Output a make title command. If the abstract text exists, wrap it in an abstract environment. For each section in the list, output a section command with the heading, then loop through its paragraphs and append each followed by a blank line. End the document environment at the end. Example: a letter size document by Jane titled Hello will yield a complete document string containing the appropriate markup commands and text blocks.

Write a utility to generate configuration files for a service ban manager. Implement `jail(configs)`. Each configuration has a service name, an enabled flag, a filter name, a log path, a maximum retry count, a find time window, and a ban time duration. Loop through the configurations. For each one, output the service name enclosed in square brackets. On the next lines, set enabled to true or false, and output the filter directive using the filter name. Output an action directive that specifies an ip tables rule passing the service name and the port to block. Specify the log path directive. Output the maximum retry, find time, and ban time directives using their respective values. Append an ignore ip line containing a local loopback address. Leave an empty line between blocks. Return the complete string.

Build a utility to generate geographic markup files from a list of waypoints. Implement `track(waypoints)`. Each waypoint provides a name, a description, a latitude, a longitude, and an altitude. The output must start with an xml declaration and a markup root element. Inside the root, open a document element. For each waypoint, open a placemark element. Add a name element with the waypoint name and a description element with the description. Add a point element containing a coordinates element formatted as longitude comma latitude comma altitude. Close the placemark element. After processing all waypoints, close the document and root elements. Return the complete formatted string. Example: an input with a single waypoint in Paris returns an xml structure containing the point and coordinates.

Create a script to generate interface definition language files for a remote procedure call system. Implement `interface(schema)`. The schema specifies a namespace string, an array of includes, an array of structs, and a service definition. The output must start by declaring the namespace using the provided string. For each included file in the array, output an include statement. Next, iterate through the structs. For each struct, output a struct declaration with its name, and loop through its fields. Output each field with its numerical identifier, type, and name, ending with a semicolon. After the structs, output a service block using the service name. Inside the service, loop through its functions, outputting the return type, function name, and an argument list formatting the parameter types and names. Close all blocks and return the text.

Create a configuration file generator for a modern secure tunnel network. Implement `tunnel(config)`. The configuration contains a client private key, a listen port, an assigned address, a max transmission unit size, a domain name server, and an array of peers. A peer has a public key, an allowed ips string, an endpoint host, an endpoint port, and a persistent keepalive interval. The output must start with an interface section heading in brackets. Below it, add a private key line, an address line, a listen port line, a domain name server line, and a max transmission unit line using the provided values. Then loop over the array of peers. For each peer, output a peer section heading in brackets followed by a blank line. Add a public key line, an allowed ips line, an endpoint line joining the host and port with a colon, and a persistent keepalive line. Return the multi line text result.

Develop a module to format electronic data interchange messages for purchase orders. Implement `transaction(order)`. The order has a sender id, a receiver id, a control number, a date string, and a list of line items. Each line item has a quantity, a price, and a product code. The result string must start with an interchange header segment using the sender id, receiver id, and control number. Add a functional group header segment using the date string. Add a transaction set header segment. For each line item, output a baseline item data segment containing the quantity, price, and product code separated by asterisks. Add a transaction set trailer segment counting the line items. Add a functional group trailer and an interchange trailer. End each segment with a tilde character. Return the final string.

Build a generator to format text files for adding entries to a lightweight directory access protocol server. Provide `directory(entries)`. Each entry has a distinguished name, an object class array, a common name, an email address, a surname, a user password, a description string, and a telephone number. Iterate over the entries. For each entry, start with a line specifying the distinguished name. Next, add a change type line set to add. For each class in the object class array, output an object class line. Output a common name line, a surname line, and an email line using the respective values. Output a user password line containing the password. Output a description line and a telephone number line. End each entry block with an empty line. Return the full text string ready for import.

Write a tool to generate declarative cloud infrastructure code from a resource blueprint. Implement `infrastructure(blueprint)`. The blueprint contains a location string, an environment string, and a list of storage accounts. Each storage account has a name prefix, a redundancy sku, and an access tier. Start the output by declaring a param for location and a param for environment. For each storage account, output a resource declaration block. Create a unique name variable by combining the name prefix and the environment string. Output the provider type for storage. Inside the block, set the name property to the unique name, the location property to the location parameter, the sku name to the redundancy sku, and the kind to storage version two. Set the access tier property. Return the formatted file content.

Create a generator that produces configuration files for a network file sharing daemon. Implement `sharing(settings)`. The input is a global settings object and a list of share definitions. The global settings dictate a workgroup name, a server string, a security mode, and a log file path. Begin the output with a global section heading enclosed in brackets. Set the workgroup directive, the server string directive, the security directive, and the log file directive using the global properties. Append a max log size line using a fixed number. Iterate through the share definitions. Each share provides a share name, a directory path, a valid users list, a comment string, and read only and guest ok boolean flags. For each share, output the share name in brackets. Output a comment line, a path line, and a valid users line joining the list with spaces. Convert the flags to yes or no strings for the read only and guest ok directives. Return the full text.

Write a generator to produce system log management configuration files. Implement `rotation(logs)`. Each log object has a file path, a rotation frequency, a retain count, a pre rotate command, and a post rotate command. Loop through the logs. For each log, begin by outputting the file path followed by an open brace. On the next lines, output the rotation frequency, then a rotate line using the retain count, and a missing ok line. If a pre rotate command exists, open a pre rotate section, output the command on a new line, and close the section with an end script line. Do the same for a post rotate command in a post rotate section. Close the log block with a brace. Leave an empty line between configurations. Return the full text string.

Create a script generator to automate batch generation of cryptographic keys. Implement `encryption(profiles)`. Each profile specifies a key type, a key length, an expiration duration, a real name, an email address, and an optional passphrase. For each profile, begin a block containing the standard batch generation tag. Add a key type line using the provided type and a key length line using the length. Add a subkey type line and subkey length line matching the primary key. Add a name real line with the real name and a name email line with the email address. Set an expire date line using the expiration duration. If a passphrase exists, add a passphrase line. End the block with a commit tag. Join all profiles with a blank line. Return the full script string.

Create a tool to assemble client connection configurations for remote access. Expose `access(hosts)`. Each host object contains a short alias, a real hostname, a username, an identity file path, a port number, and a forward agent boolean. Iterate over the host objects. For each host, start with a line specifying the host alias. On the following lines, indent and specify the host name directive using the real hostname. Add a user directive using the username. If a port is provided, add a port directive using the port number. Add an identity file directive pointing to the path. If the forward agent boolean is true, add a forward agent directive set to yes, otherwise set it to no. Separate each host block with an empty line. Return the multiline configuration text.

Write a utility to generate startup menu files for a network booting environment. Expose `boot(menu)`. The menu object has a default label, a timeout value, a menu title string, and a list of boot entries. The output must start by setting the default directive to the default label and the timeout directive to the timeout value. Output a menu title directive using the title string. For each boot entry, there is a label string, a kernel path, an init ram disk path, and an array of append parameters. Output a label directive using the label string. On the next lines, indent and output a kernel directive with the kernel path, followed by an append directive that lists the init ram disk path and joins the append parameters with spaces. Separate each entry block with an empty line and return the result.

Build a generator to create linux desktop entry files for application menus. Define `launcher(app)`. The app object has a display name, a generic name, a comment string, an executable path, an icon path, a terminal boolean, an array of categories, and an array of mime types. The output must start with a desktop entry header in brackets. Output a type directive set to application. Output a name directive, a generic name directive, and a comment directive using their respective strings. Output an exec directive using the executable path and an icon directive using the icon path. Output a terminal directive converted to a true or false string. Join the categories array with semicolons and append a trailing semicolon for the categories directive. Do the same for the mime type directive. Return the text file content.

Build a script to generate page description language files for drawing basic shapes. Implement `postscript(shapes)`. The input is a page width, a page height, and a list of shape objects. Begin the output with the standard postscript version header. Output a bounding box line using the width and height. Output a line to translate the origin to the center of the page. For each shape in the list, if it is a rectangle, output lines to set the rgb color, move to its starting coordinates, construct lines to its width and height, close the path, and fill it. If it is a circle, output the rgb color, push the center coordinates and radius, draw an arc from zero to three hundred sixty degrees, and fill it. Finally, output a show page command and an end of file indicator. Return the complete string.

Write a function `generate(playlist)` that creates an extended audio playlist format string. The input contains a master title, a creator name, an export date, a software version, a default genre, and a list of track objects. Begin the string with a header line combining the extended playlist marker and the software version. Follow this with a descriptive comment line showing the master title, creator, and export date. Add a global tag line specifying the default genre for the list. For each track, output a runtime information line containing the track duration in seconds, the artist name, and the song title. Below that, output the file path by combining the track folder, file name, and file extension. Additionally, output a custom tag line for each track showing its file size in megabytes and audio bitrate. At the end of the file, append a summary comment stating the total number of tracks. Finally, append another comment calculating and displaying the total playlist duration in minutes. Example input includes a creator named Alice, a software version of two point zero, and a track with two hundred seconds.

Write a function `slice(job)` that outputs machine instructions for a three dimensional printer. The input provides a material name, measurement units, target temperatures for the printing bed and extruder nozzle, a print speed multiplier, and a list of movement steps. Initialize the file with a comment declaring the material name and the print speed multiplier. Add a command to set the measurement units. Construct a command to set and wait for the bed temperature. Construct another command to set and wait for the nozzle temperature. Add a homing command that resets the machine axes specified in a homing list parameter. Loop through the movement steps, outputting a linear move command that specifies the x, y, and z coordinates along with the movement speed. If a step involves pushing plastic, build a dedicated extrusion command specifying the extrusion amount and speed. Include a fan speed command if the step specifies a cooling percentage. Finish the script with a concluding comment reporting the total number of movement steps processed. Example input includes a material name of plastic, measurement units of millimeters, and a bed temperature of sixty.

Write a function `fetch(system)` that produces a terminal status screen string. The input contains a username, hostname, operating system name, operating system version, kernel version, days and hours of uptime, package count, package manager name, shell name, display width, display height, and desktop environment name. Construct a top banner combining the username and hostname separated by an at symbol. Create a line for the operating system combining the name and version. Create a line for the kernel version. Construct an uptime line showing the days and hours. Build a package line combining the total package count and the package manager used. Add a line for the shell name. Build a screen resolution line showing the display width and display height. Add a line for the desktop environment. Conclude with a system memory line calculating the percentage of memory used out of a total amount. Example input includes a username of admin, an operating system name of Linux, and a package count of one thousand.

Write a function `dialplan(context)` that creates a telephone routing script. The input specifies a context name, a primary extension number, a caller identification name, a greeting sound file, a destination technology, a destination peer, a timeout value, and a voicemail box identifier. Start the output by wrapping the context name in square brackets. Write a step to answer the call at the given extension. Add a step to set the caller identification name variable for the extension. Add a step to play back the greeting sound file. Create a dial step combining the destination technology, destination peer, and timeout value. Include a step to log a warning message to the console containing the primary extension number. Include a step to route the call to the specified voicemail box if the dial fails. Finish with a step to hang up the call at the given extension. Example input includes a context name of incoming, a primary extension number of one hundred, and a destination technology of session initiation protocol.

Write a function `mounts(drives)` that builds a disk mounting configuration file. The input contains a machine hostname, a backup server address, a backup path, a swap partition device, a temporary folder size, and a list of volume objects containing device identifiers and mount point directories. Begin the file with a comment line indicating it was generated for the provided machine hostname. Output a swap entry using the swap partition device. Output a temporary file system entry specifying the temporary folder size in the options. Output a network file system entry combining the backup server address and backup path as the source. Include a read only network entry combining the backup server address and a public share path. Loop through the volume objects, and for each one, output a descriptive comment naming the mount point directory. Then, output a line with the device identifier, mount point directory, and default options. Finally, append a concluding comment stating the total number of physical volumes processed. Example input includes a machine hostname of server one, a swap partition device of slash dev slash sdb, and a temporary folder size of four gigabytes.

Write a function `menu(config)` that builds an extensible markup language file for a desktop application menu. The input holds a root menu identifier, a root menu label, a terminal application command, a web browser command, a file manager command, a text editor command, a separator label, and an exit command. Output the opening tag for the menu, inserting the identifier and label into their respective attributes. Create an item tag and execution action for the terminal application command, placing it inside a command tag. Create a similar execution block for the web browser command. Create a third execution block for the file manager command. Create a fourth execution block for the text editor command. Output a separator tag specifying the separator label in its attribute. Create a final execution block for the exit command. Output the closing tag for the root menu, embedding the identifier in a trailing comment. Example input provides a root menu identifier of desktop menu, a terminal application command of xterm, and a separator label of System.

Write a function `prompt(theme)` that builds a multiline configuration file for a terminal prompt framework. The input defines a theme name, a user color, a host color, a directory color, a repository color, an exit code color, a prompt symbol color, and a symbol character. Output a line setting the theme name variable. Output a line assigning the user text segment with the user color. Output a line assigning the host text segment with the host color. Output a line assigning the directory path segment with the directory color. Output a line assigning the version control segment with the repository color. Output a line assigning the error code segment with the exit code color. Output a line setting the primary symbol segment using the prompt symbol color and the symbol character. Finally, output an activation command calling the framework initialization with the theme name. Example input includes a theme name of spaceship, a user color of blue, and a symbol character of arrow.

Write a function `wiki(document)` that constructs a text document using enterprise wiki formatting. The input provides a main heading, an author username, a summary paragraph, a warning panel title, a warning message, a code snippet language, a code snippet body, and an issue ticket identifier. Output the main heading formatted as a level one heading. Add a line mentioning the author by wrapping their username in the appropriate mention brackets. Write the summary paragraph enclosed in formatting characters to make it italicized. Construct the warning panel by placing the warning panel title into the macro parameters and wrapping the warning message. Create a code block macro using the code snippet language in the parameters and wrap the code snippet body inside it. Output a hyperlink to the internal tracker using the issue ticket identifier. Include a status macro displaying the text in progress colored yellow. Finally, add a footer line stating the document was generated for the author username. Example input includes a main heading of Project Status, an author username of jsmith, and an issue ticket identifier of bug one two three.

Write a function `provision(environment)` that creates a ruby based virtual machine configuration script. The input specifies a configuration version, an operating system box name, a machine hostname, a virtual network address, a host folder path, a guest folder path, a provider name, and an allocated memory size in megabytes. Open the configuration block using the configuration version string. Set the machine box name enclosed in quotes. Set the machine hostname in quotes. Define a private network interface assigning the virtual network address. Configure a synchronized folder mapping the host folder path to the guest folder path. Open a provider block using the provider name. Inside the provider block, set the memory allocation to the specified megabytes. Finally, add a shell provisioner command that prints a greeting message containing the machine hostname. Example input includes an operating system box name of ubuntu, an allocated memory size of two thousand, and a virtual network address of ten dot zero dot zero dot five.

Write a function `build(project)` that writes a cross platform compilation script. The input specifies a minimum required tool version, a project name, a project version, a programming language standard year, an output executable name, a source file name, an external library name, and an installation directory path. Start with the minimum required version command using the tool version. Add the project command combining the project name and the project version. Set the language standard variable to the standard year. Create the add executable command linking the output executable name with the source file name. Create a target link libraries command linking the output executable name with the external library name. Create a target include directories command linking the output executable name with an include folder. Create an install command pointing the output executable name to the installation directory path. Finally, add a status message command printing the project name and project version. Example input includes a project name of Calculator, a programming language standard year of seventeen, and a tool version of three point ten.

Write a function `routing(peer)` that constructs a border gateway protocol configuration snippet. The input specifies a local autonomous system number, a router identifier address, a neighbor internet address, a remote autonomous system number, a neighbor description text, an address family identifier, a network prefix string, and a routing map name. Start the block with the router declaration using the local autonomous system number. Set the router identifier address. Define the neighbor using its internet address and the remote autonomous system number. Add the neighbor description text referencing the neighbor internet address. Enter the address family configuration block using the address family identifier. Declare the network prefix string to be advertised. Apply the routing map by name to the neighbor internet address in the inbound direction. Finally, activate the neighbor using its internet address. Example input includes a local autonomous system number of six five zero zero one, a router identifier address of one dot one dot one dot one, and a network prefix string of ten dot zero dot zero dot zero slash twenty four.

Write a function `subnet(allocation)` that generates a dynamic host allocation configuration block. The input contains a subnet network address, a subnet mask, a starting address for the pool, an ending address for the pool, a default gateway address, a domain name server address, a local domain name, and a lease time integer. Begin by declaring the subnet network address and subnet mask, opening a block with a brace. Output the address pool range using the starting and ending addresses. Output the routers option with the default gateway address. Output the domain name servers option with the domain name server address. Output the domain name option wrapped in quotes. Output the default lease time using the lease time integer. Output the maximum lease time by multiplying the lease time integer by two. Finally, add a descriptive comment summarizing the subnet network address and default gateway address before closing the block. Example input provides a subnet network address of one ninety two dot one sixty eight dot one dot zero, a subnet mask of two five five dot two five five dot two five five dot zero, and a lease time integer of six hundred.

Write a function `launcher(application)` that constructs a linux application shortcut file. The input contains an application type, a display name, a tooltip comment, an executable path, startup arguments, an icon identifier, a startup notification boolean, and a category tag. Start the file with the standard desktop entry header enclosed in brackets. Add the application type. Add the display name. Add the tooltip comment. Combine the executable path and startup arguments on the execution line. Add the icon identifier. Add the startup notification boolean. Append the category tag to the categories line, ensuring a trailing semicolon is present. Finally, add a generic string associating the display name with the category tag in a custom keywords line. Example input includes an application type of Application, a display name of Text Editor, and an executable path of slash usr slash bin slash nano.

Write a function `window(setup)` that generates a tiling window manager configuration file. The input includes a modifier key name, a terminal command, a launcher command, a font family name, a font size, a display output name, a screen resolution string, and a background image path. Set the modifier variable to the modifier key name. Set the terminal variable to the terminal command. Set the menu variable to the launcher command. Set the text font using the font family name and font size. Bind the modifier and enter key to execute the terminal variable. Bind the modifier and the letter D to execute the menu variable. Configure the display output using its name and screen resolution string. Configure the display output to use the background image path stretched across the screen. Example input includes a modifier key name of Mod Four, a terminal command of alacritty, and a font size of twelve.

Write a function `syslog(routing)` that creates a system logging daemon rule block. The input specifies a text logging facility, a text severity level, an output template name, a custom formatting string, a destination address, a destination port, a local fallback file path, and a queue directory path. Define a global work directory using the queue directory path before loading the module. Load the forwarding output module. Define a formatting template using the output template name and the custom formatting string. Open a conditional block checking if the incoming facility and severity match the input parameters. Inside the block, write a forwarding action utilizing the destination address, destination port, and the defined template. Add an action queue configuration using the queue directory path. Add a local file action using the fallback file path. Add a stop command. Close the conditional block and append a comment mentioning the text logging facility. Example input provides a text logging facility of authpriv, a text severity level of error, and a destination port of five one four.

Build a boarding pass text generator. The entry function `ticket(flight)` takes a travel information object and returns a formatted itinerary. Break the logic into helpers for passenger, flight, boarding, and routing information. The passenger section creates two lines: one combining the first name and last name, and one for the frequent flyer number. The flight section outputs three separate lines: the airline name, the flight number, and the departure date. The boarding section generates three lines detailing the gate number, the seat assignment, and the boarding time. The routing section summarizes two lines: one combining the origin airport code and destination airport code, and one for the flight duration. Each helper must return an array of formatted strings to be joined by newlines. For example, a flight on Delta number five produces one line for Delta and another for flight five.

Develop a plain text receipt generator for a restaurant. The function `receipt(order)` transforms a dining order object into a printable string. Create separate functions to format the restaurant header, order details, item lines, and financial totals. The header must generate three distinct lines: the restaurant name, the street address, and the phone number. The order details produce three lines detailing the server name, the table number, and the date. For each ordered item, format a line showing the quantity, item name, and price. Finally, the totals section generates four separate lines summarizing the subtotal, the tax amount, the tip suggestion, and the final total. Concatenate these parts with newline characters to form the full receipt. For example, a subtotal of fifty and tax of five should produce one line for fifty subtotal and another for five tax.

Build a text generator for software release notes. The entry function `release(version)` accepts a version data object and returns a structured text document. Implement helpers for the header, breaking changes, new features, and bug fixes. The header generates three individual lines for the version number, the release date, and the primary author. The breaking changes section formats sentences combining the affected component, a description of the change, and the required migration step. The features section highlights each enhancement by generating a line combining the module name, the enhancement description, and the related issue number. The fixes section notes each bug by combining the bug description, the resolution, and the reporter name. Combine all these generated lines to form the changelog. Assuming multiple features and fixes, this ensures many formatted strings. A release by Alice on Monday produces one line for Alice and one for Monday.

Create a tool to summarize the events of a board game turn. The function `summarize(round)` processes the round data into a descriptive paragraph. Use helper routines to format the round overview, player actions, resource changes, and current standings. The overview generates three separate sentences stating the round number, the current phase, and the active player name. The actions section formats a sentence for each action describing which player performed what action type against which target. The resource section details three distinct lines for changes in wood counts, clay counts, and wheat counts. The standings section outputs two sentences: one for the first place player and their score, and one for the second place player. Piece these sentences together into a continuous narrative. If round three is in the building phase, it generates one sentence for round three and another for building phase.

Build a personalized daily horoscope text generator. The function `horoscope(reading)` converts an astrological data object into a reading paragraph. Write helper functions for the sign identity, date information, core predictions, and lucky items. The sign identity formats three separate sentences: the zodiac sign, its elemental group, and its ruling planet. The date information generates two sentences combining the current calendar date and a specific lucky time of day. The prediction section describes multiple life categories, generating a sentence for each combining the category, a descriptive text, and an intensity level. The lucky items section creates three lines listing a lucky number, an auspicious color, and a recommended gemstone. Combine these elements into a cohesive fortune paragraph. A fire sign Aries produces one sentence stating it is Aries and another stating its element is fire.

Create a text message formatter for monthly banking summaries. The entry function `sms(statement)` takes a financial object and returns a compact multiline alert string. Implement helpers to format account identifiers, balance summaries, major expenses, and budget alerts. The account identifier creates three lines combining the bank name, the last four digits of the account, and the statement month. The balance summary details three individual lines for the starting balance, the ending balance, and the currency type. The major expense section highlights two sentences: the top merchant name, and combining the amount spent with the transaction date. The budget alert specifies three lines for the limit type, the warning threshold, and the current spending. Concatenate these brief sentences with newlines for the final text. A starting balance of six hundred and ending at five hundred produces two distinct lines.

topic: Mobile App Deep Link URI Builder
text_es: Create a custom uniform resource identifier string builder for a mobile application. The function `deeplink(route)` converts navigation parameters into a documented multiline text block describing the link details. Implement helpers to construct the scheme, the resource path, the query parameters, and the fallback details. The scheme formats three distinct lines detailing the internet protocol, the app identifier, and the region code. The resource path generates two lines combining the resource type and the specific resource identifier. The query parameters format three lines describing the marketing campaign, the traffic source, and the advertising medium. The fallback details format three individual lines for a web address, a store identifier, and a language code. Join these components with newlines to form the descriptive text. A protocol of myapp and region us formats a line for myapp and a line for us.

Write a descriptive text generator for sommelier tasting notes. The entry function `tasting(wine)` accepts a tasting evaluation object and returns a formatted multiline paragraph. Use separate helpers to describe the wine identity, visual characteristics, olfactory notes, and palate profile. The identity formats three separate sentences detailing the harvest vintage year, the grape varietal, and the wine region. The visual characteristics describe three individual lines outlining the liquid clarity, the color intensity, and the specific hue. The olfactory notes detail three lines describing the condition, the aroma intensity, and the specific aromatic descriptors. The palate profile summarizes three distinct lines identifying the sweetness level, the acidity, and the tannin structure. Weave these twelve sentences together to produce a continuous tasting note document. A vintage of twenty ten from region bordeaux starts with a sentence for twenty ten and another for bordeaux.

Write `interpret(reading)`. The input contains a seeker name, past card, present card, future card, deck name, reader name, spread type, and session date. It returns a single large text block made of several sentences forming a complete reading. The first sentence greets the seeker name. The second sentence names the spread type. The third sentence credits the reader name and the deck name. The fourth sentence reveals the past card. The fifth sentence explains the present card. The sixth sentence predicts the future card. The seventh sentence notes the session date. The final sentence creates a custom blessing using the seeker name.

Write `format(dive)`. Input includes location, site, date, max depth, average depth, bottom time, start pressure, and end pressure. It constructs a text summary array. Line one combines location and site. Line two states the date. Line three reports the max depth. Line four lists the average depth. Line five shows the bottom time. Line six displays the start pressure. Line seven shows the end pressure. The last line calculates gas used by subtracting the end pressure from the start pressure and formats the result.

Write `summarize(encounter)`. Input has a campaign name, environment type, party level, difficulty rating, total experience, average hit points, a list of monsters, and an encounter date. It produces an array of text lines. Line one announces the campaign name and encounter date. Line two describes the environment type. Line three states the party level. Line four warns of the difficulty rating. Line five states the total experience. Line six displays the average hit points. For each monster in the list, it appends a line combining its name and initiative. The last line calculates and states the total number of monsters.

Write `export(contact)`. Input holds a callsign, band, frequency, mode, signal sent, signal received, operator name, and station location. It outputs a list of text records. Record one links the callsign and operator name. Record two states the station location. Record three specifies the band. Record four formats the frequency. Record five declares the mode. Record six logs the signal sent. Record seven logs the signal received. Record eight displays a verification code generated by combining the callsign and frequency.

Write `build(cache)`. Input has a cache name, owner name, container size, latitude, longitude, difficulty rating, terrain rating, and a hint text. It generates an array of strings representing a geocache. The first string introduces the cache name. The second string credits the owner name. The third string specifies the container size. The fourth string formats the latitude. The fifth string formats the longitude. The sixth string combines difficulty rating and terrain rating. The seventh string warns before providing the hint text. The eighth string provides a fake checksum by adding the difficulty rating and terrain rating.

Write `propose(trade)`. Input contains an offering team, receiving team, league name, week number, offered player, requested player, deadline day, and commissioner name. It produces an array of message sentences for fantasy sports. Sentence one greets the receiving team from the offering team. Sentence two mentions the league name. Sentence three references the week number. Sentence four offers the offered player. Sentence five demands the requested player. Sentence six sets the deadline day. Sentence seven copies the commissioner name. Sentence eight signs off using the offering team name.

Write `describe(pattern)`. Input has a pattern name, juggler name, prop count, prop type, starting hand, maximum height, average height, and duration seconds. It returns an array of descriptive lines. Line one links the pattern name and juggler name. Line two specifies the prop count. Line three names the prop type. Line four indicates the starting hand. Line five states the maximum height. Line six shows the average height. Line seven logs the duration seconds. Line eight calculates total throws by multiplying duration seconds by prop count.

Write `build(menu)`. Input includes a server host, server port, menu title, admin email, welcome text, footer text, total items, and generation date. It creates an array of gopher text lines. Line one formats an info item for the menu title. Line two formats an info item for the server host and server port. Line three links to the admin email. Line four displays the welcome text. Line five states the total items. Line six displays the footer text. Line seven logs the generation date. Line eight creates a fake ending marker combining the server host and total items.

Write `format(page)`. Input contains a page title, author name, contact email, license type, creation date, welcome message, primary link url, and primary link description. It returns an array of text lines formatted for the gemini protocol. Line one creates a large heading with the page title. Line two credits the author name. Line three provides the contact email. Line four states the license type. Line five notes the creation date. Line six formats the welcome message. Line seven creates a link line using the primary link url and primary link description. Line eight generates a footer using the author name and creation date.

Write `format(recipe)`. Input includes a beer style, batch volume, original gravity, final gravity, alcohol percentage, bitterness ibu, boil time, and primary yeast. It produces an array of recipe lines. Line one pairs the beer style and batch volume. Line two targets the original gravity. Line three targets the final gravity. Line four estimates the alcohol percentage. Line five calculates the bitterness ibu. Line six requires the boil time. Line seven pitches the primary yeast. Line eight generates a label string combining the beer style and alcohol percentage.

Write `guide(garden)`. Input contains a bed name, hardiness zone, frost date, sun exposure, soil type, water frequency, primary crop, and companion plant. It builds an array of guide strings. String one introduces the bed name and hardiness zone. String two warns about the frost date. String three specifies the sun exposure. String four requires the soil type. String five dictates the water frequency. String six highlights the primary crop. String seven suggests the companion plant. String eight calculates a harvest estimate by combining the primary crop and frost date.

Write `summarize(bout)`. Input specifies a red fencer, blue fencer, weapon type, pool number, referee name, time limit, red score, and blue score. It constructs an array of bout lines. Line one pits the red fencer against the blue fencer. Line two specifies the weapon type. Line three notes the pool number. Line four names the referee name. Line five sets the time limit. Line six reports the red score. Line seven reports the blue score. Line eight calculates the point difference by subtracting the blue score from the red score.

Create an entry function `summarize(tanks)`. The input is a list of items, each having a tank number, a species name, a temperature, a ph level, a filter status, a lighting mode, and a feeding time. Return a multi-line text report. Start with a main header stating the total number of tanks. Add a subheader stating the daily report is generated. Loop through each tank. Output a line announcing the tank number and the species. Output a line detailing the temperature and ph level. Output a line showing the filter status and lighting mode. If the temperature is below twenty or above twenty eight, add a line warning about the critical temperature in that specific tank. If the ph level is below seven, add a line noting that the water in the specific tank is acidic. After the loop, add a footer stating the total count of active filters. Add a final line stating the feeding time from the first tank as the next scheduled facility feeding. Example input: a list with one item having tank number one, species clownfish, temperature twenty five, ph level eight, filter status active, lighting mode day, and feeding time noon. Example output: a text containing the headers, the tank details, and the calculated footers.

Create an entry function `report(rides)`. The input is a list of items, each having a ride name, a wait time, an operational status, a maximum capacity, a fast track availability, and a safety inspector name. Return a multi-line text report. Begin with a header stating the total number of rides being reported. Add a line stating the official theme park daily status. Loop through each ride. Add a line naming the ride and its current operational status. Add a line detailing the current wait time and the maximum capacity. Add a line stating the name of the assigned safety inspector for that ride. If the fast track availability is true, add a line highlighting that fast track is open for the specific ride. If the wait time exceeds sixty minutes, add a line warning that the specific ride has a severe delay. After the loop, calculate the average wait time and add a footer line stating this average. Conclude with a final line stating that the report is complete for the specific total number of rides. Example input: a list with one item having ride name rollercoaster, wait time forty five, operational status running, maximum capacity one hundred, fast track availability true, and safety inspector name John. Example output: a text containing the headers, the ride details on multiple lines, and the summary footers.

Create an entry function `generate(rows)`. The input is a list of items, each with a row number, a stitch type, a stitch count, a yarn color, a needle size, and a tension level. Return a multi-line pattern guide. Start with a header announcing the new knitting project. Add a line stating the total number of rows in the pattern. For each row, add a line announcing the row number and the yarn color to use. Add a line instructing to perform the stitch count of the specific stitch type. Add a line recommending the specific needle size for this section. Add a line specifying the tension level required for the specific row number. If the stitch count is greater than fifty, add a line advising to use a stitch marker after twenty five stitches on that row. After the loop, add a footer line stating the project is ready for blocking. Add a final line congratulating the knitter on finishing the project with the specific total rows count. Example input: a list with one item having row number one, stitch type purl, stitch count sixty, yarn color red, needle size five, and tension level tight. Example output: a multi-line string with the project headers, the detailed instructions for each row, and the congratulatory footers.

Create an entry function `format(intersections)`. The input is a list of items, each with an intersection name, a north south duration, an east west duration, a pedestrian crossing time, a peak hour modifier, and a camera active flag. Return a multi-line timing report. Start with a main header for the city traffic control system. Add a line stating the number of monitored intersections. For each intersection, output a line naming the intersection. Output a line detailing the north south duration and the east west duration in seconds. Output a line showing the pedestrian crossing time. Output a line stating the peak hour modifier percentage. If the camera active flag is true, add a line stating that traffic enforcement cameras are recording at the specific intersection name. After the loop, calculate the total pedestrian crossing time across all intersections and output a footer stating this sum. Output a final line confirming that the specific number of intersections are synchronized. Example input: a list with one item having intersection name main street, north south duration forty, east west duration thirty, pedestrian crossing time fifteen, peak hour modifier ten, and camera active flag true. Example output: a text string with the system headers, the intersection timing details, and the summary footers.

Create an entry function `profile(animals)`. The input is a list of items, each with an animal name, a species, a breed, an age in months, a weight in pounds, and a temperament description. Return a multi-line adoption showcase text. Start with a header welcoming people to the weekly pet adoption drive. Add a line stating the number of animals looking for homes today. Loop through the list. Output a line introducing the animal name, their species, and their breed. Output a line stating they are a certain age in months and weigh a certain weight in pounds. Output a line describing their personality using the temperament description. Output a line asking to come meet the specific animal name in person. If the age in months is less than six, add a line noting that the specific animal name is a young baby and requires extra training. After the loop, add a footer line providing the shelter address. Add a final line reminding that adopting any of the specific number of animals saves lives. Example input: a list with one item having animal name buddy, species dog, breed beagle, age in months four, weight in pounds ten, and temperament description playful and energetic. Example output: a text containing the adoption drive headers, the animal profiles, and the shelter footers.

Create an entry function `catalog(finds)`. The input is a list of items, each with a specimen number, a mass in grams, a structural classification, a latitude, a longitude, and a weathering grade. Return a multi-line expedition field report. Start with a header for the desert meteorite recovery expedition. Add a line stating the total number of specimens recovered. For each find, output a line naming the specimen number and its structural classification. Output a line stating the mass in grams. Output a line detailing the exact location at the specific latitude and longitude. Output a line noting the weathering grade observed on the crust. If the mass in grams exceeds one thousand, add a line declaring a major discovery for the specific specimen number. After the loop, add a footer line indicating the end of the daily log with the specific total specimens secured. Add a final line stating that all samples are sealed for transport. Example input: a list with one item having specimen number rock one, mass in grams five hundred, structural classification chondrite, latitude forty five, longitude ninety, and weathering grade moderate. Example output: a text string containing the expedition headers, the specimen details, and the daily log footers.

Create an entry function `document(elevators)`. The input is a list of items, each with an elevator identifier, a floors served count, a cable condition rating, a door operation status, a last service date, and a technician name. Return a multi-line building inspection report. Start with a header for the monthly elevator safety inspection. Add a line stating the total number of units inspected. For each elevator, output a line identifying the elevator identifier. Output a line stating it serves a specific floors served count. Output a line reporting the cable condition rating. Output a line describing the door operation status. Output a line noting the last service date and the previous technician name. If the cable condition rating is poor, add a line demanding immediate out of service lock down for the specific elevator identifier. After the loop, add a footer line signing off the current inspection for the specific total units. Add a final line stating the next scheduled maintenance date. Example input: a list with one item having elevator identifier car a, floors served count ten, cable condition rating good, door operation status smooth, last service date january first, and technician name bob. Example output: a text string containing the inspection headers, the unit status logs, and the sign off footers.

topic: Musical Theatre Lighting Cue Sheet Builder
text_es: Create an entry function `build(cues)`. The input is a list of items, each with a cue number, a scene name, a fade transition time, a stage focus area, a color gel name, and an intensity percentage. Return a multi-line technical theater cue sheet. Start with a header for the lighting booth operator guide. Add a line stating the total number of lighting cues for the act. Iterate through each cue. Output a line announcing the cue number for the specific scene name. Output a line instructing a fade transition time in seconds. Output a line directing the spotlight to the specific stage focus area. Output a line requiring the insertion of the specific color gel name. Output a line setting the lamp to the specific intensity percentage. If the intensity percentage is one hundred, add a line warning of extreme heat on the specific stage focus area. After the loop, add a footer line declaring the end of the act after the specific total cues. Add a final line instructing the crew to reset for intermission. Example input: a list with one item having cue number one, scene name opening number, fade transition time five, stage focus area center stage, color gel name warm amber, and intensity percentage eighty. Example output: a text string containing the operator headers, the detailed lighting cues, and the intermission footers.

topic: Debate Tournament Motion and Speaker Announcement
text_es: Create an entry function `announce(debates)`. The input is a list of items, each with a room number, a motion text, a proposition team name, an opposition team name, a chief adjudicator, and a speaking format. Return a multi-line tournament round announcement. Begin with a header calling all debaters to the main hall. Add a line stating the total number of matches in this round. Loop through each debate. Output a line directing participants to the specific room number. Output a line declaring the motion text to be debated. Output a line announcing the proposition team name. Output a line announcing the opposition team name. Output a line introducing the chief adjudicator for the room. Output a line stating the rules follow the specific speaking format. If the speaking format is iron person, add a line noting that a speaker is debating alone in the specific room number. After the loop, add a footer line stating the preparation time has started for the specific total matches. Add a final line wishing all teams the best of luck. Example input: a list with one item having room number one zero one, motion text ban plastic bags, proposition team alpha, opposition team beta, chief adjudicator jane, and speaking format standard. Example output: a text containing the main hall headers, the match announcements, and the preparation footers.

topic: Paleontology Dig Site Fossil Record Summary
text_es: Create an entry function `record(specimens)`. The input is a list of items, each with a field number, a bone type, a species name, a completeness percentage, a grid coordinate, and an excavation tool used. Return a multi-line excavation field log. Start with a header for the seasonal paleontology dig site. Add a line stating the total number of specimens uncovered. Loop through each specimen. Output a line noting the field number and the bone type. Output a line identifying the proposed species name. Output a line showing the completeness percentage of the fossil. Output a line detailing the exact grid coordinate in the trench. Output a line recording the excavation tool used to extract it. If the completeness percentage is greater than ninety, add a line marking the specific field number as a rare museum quality find. After the loop, add a footer line stating the trench is secured for the night protecting the specific total specimens. Add a final line reminding the team to catalog the plaster jackets. Example input: a list with one item having field number one, bone type femur, species name velociraptor, completeness percentage eighty five, grid coordinate a five, and excavation tool used brush. Example output: a text containing the site headers, the fossil extraction details, and the night security footers.

Write a function `plan(waypoints)` that converts a list of drone movement instructions into a human readable text sequence. The input is a list of waypoint objects containing a latitude number, a longitude number, an altitude in meters, a speed in meters per second, an action text, and a camera angle number. The function must return a list of text strings. Start the output with a summary sentence stating the total number of waypoints. For each waypoint, produce six separate string sentences. First, describe the movement to the latitude and longitude. Second, specify the cruise altitude. Third, detail the flight speed. Fourth, state the specific action text. Fifth, note the camera angle. Sixth, calculate and display the estimated battery drain by multiplying the speed by two. Finally, append a closing sentence indicating the drone returns to base.

Write a function `document(strata)` that processes a list of rock layer records from a core drilling operation into a list of descriptive text lines. The input is a list of layers, where each has a rock type text, a start depth number, an end depth number, a color text, a fossil inclusion text, and a grain size text. The output list must begin with a title line stating the number of layers analyzed. For each layer, generate six lines of text. The first line must state the rock type. The second line notes the color. The third line describes the start depth. The fourth line describes the end depth. The fifth line calculates the layer thickness by subtracting the start from the end depth. The sixth line documents the fossil inclusion and grain size. End the output with a final line stating the analysis is complete.

Write a function `label(specimens)` that generates exhibition label texts for preserved plant samples. The input is a list of specimen items, each with a plant species text, a botanical family text, a collection region, a collector name, a collection year, and a preservation method text. The function returns a list of formatted text lines. Start with an exhibition header string stating the total specimen count. For each specimen, append six strings to the list. The first string states the species. The second string states the botanical family. The third string details the region where the plant was found. The fourth string credits the collector name. The fifth string calculates the age of the specimen by subtracting the collection year from the current year. The sixth string records the preservation method. Write `mix(formulas)` to generate text guides for hair stylists. The input is a list of dye formulas detailing the client name, the base shade, the developer volume, and the processing time. Output a flat array of mixing sentences. For each formula, first push a client string combining the client name and the base shade. If the developer volume is ten, push a deposit string using the base shade and the developer volume, followed by a timing string citing the client name.
